does: Draws most of the salt out of salt cod by leaving it in cold water that is changed again and again, so that the fish tastes of cod and not only of salt, and can be cooked on its own.
how: Rinse the surface salt off the pieces under cold water.
Lay the pieces skin side up in a deep dish and cover them with plenty of cold water. Keep the dish in the fridge.
Change the water several times, and leave thick pieces longer than thin ones.
Taste a small flake from the thickest part. Stop when it tastes lightly seasoned, and go on if it still tastes of brine.
Drain the pieces and pat them dry before they are cooked.

cues.text: A flake from the thickest part tastes lightly salted, like seasoned fish and not like brine.
The flesh has swelled and gone soft and springy, where it was stiff and hard before.

mistakes.mistake: Soaking at room temperature, where the fish spoils and turns slimy before it loses its salt.
mistakes.fix: Soak it in the fridge and change the water often.

mistakes.mistake: Tasting the thin end only, which loses its salt first.
mistakes.fix: Taste a flake from the thickest part.

mistakes.mistake: Salting the dish as usual afterwards, so that it ends up far too salty.
mistakes.fix: Taste the fish and the sauce before adding any salt.

comes_after.why: The loose salt on the surface is rinsed off before the long soak.

variant_of.differs: The aim is to take salt out and not to swell the food. The water is changed again and again, and the cook tastes the thickest part to decide when it is done, not the clock.
